ops.title: Linux amd64 support for cookiesync (ABWC contract on a private single-user VM)
ops.description:
Requested by Yasyf ("cant we just use cookiesync there too? make it work on linux?") as part of the Orca per-workspace Linux VM project. Lane: cookiesync-linux, branch yasyf/cookiesync-linux, worktree /Users/yasyf/.orca/workspaces/cookiesync/cookiesync-linux.

Scope: implement the command contract agent-browser-with-cookies 0.12.2 consumes on Linux amd64 — `cookiesync requestor`, `auth --reason`, `cookies --format playwright|webstorage|header -- HOST...`, `bridge open --json` / `bridge stop` — with Linux Chromium cookie crypto, profile discovery, daemon supervision, Linux release assets and a CI smoke on synthetic profiles. Darwin signing, Keychain and Touch ID behavior stay unchanged. Never silently lower browser encryption; never weaken the Mac's remote-client trust.

Constraints: no Mac install/update/restart/signal, no local VM/container, no real cookies or credentials read, no tests that touch the Mac's live synckit/cookiesync globals (CI is the verifier). ROOT owns merges, tags and releases; this lane stops at a reviewable PR with green exact-head CI.

Scratch + recon + design: /private/tmp/orca-linux-releases.eLT1vT/cookiesync-linux/. Final report: /private/tmp/orca-linux-releases.eLT1vT/cookiesync-linux-implementation.md.

ops.text: Source PR open on yasyf/cookiesync with a real body, not draft, not merged, not tagged
Every CI run on the exact PR head is green, including a Linux job
Linux CI smoke covers requestor/daemon, synthetic cookie extraction, all three formats, browser seeding and bridge open/stop
Darwin build, signing config and Keychain/Touch ID code paths unchanged in behavior
Owner decisions (key backend, consent stand-in) reported with 2-4 options and a conservative default implemented meanwhile
Bus contract post made and final report written to disk
